name: Insolvency Professional
title: Insolvency Professional (IBBI)
intro: From a graduate or professional qualification to an IBBI-registered insolvency professional: the experience route or the Graduate Insolvency Programme, the Limited Insolvency Examination, IPA enrolment, the pre-registration course, then registration and an Authorisation for Assignment.

phases.title: Graduate or professional qualification
phases.summary: Law, CA, CS, CMA or management.
points: Any Class 12 stream works; you qualify later through a professional qualification plus experience, or the GIP.
Common bases: advocate, CA, CS, CMA or a management degree.

phases.title: Experience route or GIP
phases.summary: Build the years the IP Regulations list, or join IBBI's Graduate Insolvency Programme.
points: Experience route: a professional membership or degree plus the years of professional/managerial experience the IP Regulations list (for example 10 years for professionals).
Graduate route: IBBI's two-year Graduate Insolvency Programme for young graduates and professionals with less than 10 years' experience.
A fresh graduate cannot enter directly through the experience route.

phases.title: Limited Insolvency Examination
phases.summary: Insolvency law, corporate law, finance and valuation basics.
points: The Limited Insolvency Examination is the qualifying exam for IPs; its syllabus and format are published for IBBI.
It covers insolvency law, corporate law, finance and valuation basics.
You must enrol with an IPA within 12 months of passing.

phases.title: Enrol with an IPA and take its course
phases.summary: Insolvency Professional Agencies enrol and supervise IPs.
points: IPAs are front-line regulators that enrol and supervise IPs; IBBI lists them.
Complete the IPA's pre-registration educational course.
Then apply to IBBI for registration.

phases.title: IBBI registration and practice
phases.summary: An Authorisation for Assignment lets you take cases.
points: After IBBI registration you need an Authorisation for Assignment to take cases.
Work comes from creditors, NCLT appointments and banks; fees for each assignment are approved by creditors under IBBI rules.
Growth path: associate → IP → partner in an insolvency professional entity.
